facts.text: Turandot premiered at La Scala on 25 April 1926, about a year and a half after Puccini’s death; Franco Alfano completed the music.
facts.evidence: The music was completed by Franco Alfano  and premiered on 25 April 1926, almost a year and a half after Puccini's death.

facts.text: Diagnosed with throat cancer, Puccini begged Toscanini before leaving for treatment: “Don’t let my Turandot die.”
evidence: he was diagnosed with throat cancer
he visited Arturo Toscanini and begged him, "Don't let my Turandot die."

facts.text: Liù’s death and funeral procession were the last music Puccini composed and orchestrated. He left 36 pages of sketches for the ending.
evidence: Puccini had composed and fully orchestrated act three up until Liù's death and funeral cortege
He left behind 36 pages of sketches on 23 sheets for the end of Turandot

facts.text: At the premiere Toscanini stopped here and told the audience: “Here the opera ends, because at this point the maestro died.” The curtain came down.
evidence: Toscanini turned to the audience and announced
Here the opera ends, because at this point the maestro died

facts.text: Toscanini and Ricordi criticized Alfano’s first ending so severely that he had to write a second, strictly censored version, which Toscanini then cut by about three minutes.
evidence: After the severe criticisms by Ricordi and the conductor Arturo Toscanini, he was forced to write a second, strictly censored version
about three minutes were cut for performance by Toscanini

facts.text: Rosa Raisa, the first Turandot, said neither Puccini nor Toscanini ever pronounced the final “t” of the name.
facts.evidence: Soprano Rosa Raisa, who created the title role, said that neither Puccini nor Arturo Toscanini, who conducted the first performances, ever pronounced the final t.

facts.text: It was Schiller’s version of the tale that inspired Puccini to write the opera.
facts.evidence: It was Schiller's version that inspired Puccini to write the opera.

facts.text: Pavarotti took “Nessun dorma” far beyond the opera world with his performance for the 1990 World Cup; his single reached number 2 in the UK.
evidence: Luciano Pavarotti popularised the piece beyond the opera world in the 1990s with his performance of it for the 1990 World Cup
with Pavarotti's reaching number 2 in the UK

facts.text: The Three Tenors sang “Nessun dorma” at three more World Cup finals: 1994, 1998 and 2002.
facts.evidence: The Three Tenors performed the aria at three subsequent World Cup Finals, in 1994 in Los Angeles, 1998 in Paris, and 2002 in Yokohama.

facts.text: For many years China forbade performances of Turandot, saying it portrayed the country unfavourably.
facts.evidence: the government of the People's Republic of China forbade performance of Turandot because they said it portrayed China and the Chinese unfavourably

facts.text: Critic Joseph Kerman: “Puccini, however, did not find it; his music does nothing to rationalise the legend or illuminate the characters.”
facts.evidence: Puccini, however, did not find it; his music does nothing to rationalise the legend or illuminate the characters.

facts.text: “Del primo pianto” was sung at the premiere but cut from the first complete recording. It was later restored to most performances.
facts.evidence: Turandot's aria "Del primo pianto" was performed at the premiere but cut from the first complete recording; it was eventually restored to most performances

facts.text: Luciano Berio wrote a new completion in 2002, with the cooperation of the publisher, Ricordi.
facts.evidence: A later attempt at completing the opera was made, with the co-operation of the publishers, Ricordi, in 2002 by Luciano Berio.
